events.title: Anthropic Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 released
events.summary: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 on June 9, 2026 — its fifth-generation frontier models, split into a generally available safe build and a restricted cyberdefense variant.
events.about: Fable 5 and Mythos 5 share the same underlying model. Fable 5 is Anthropic's top generally available tier: safety classifiers route sensitive cybersecurity and biology queries to Claude Opus 4.8 instead. Mythos 5 lifts those safeguards for vetted partners in Project Glasswing — Anthropic's answer to releasing a model strong enough to help defenders without open-sourcing misuse risk. Both ship at $10/$50 per million tokens.

narrative.whyChosen: Anthropic split one frontier model into public Fable and restricted Mythos to balance capability and safety.
narrative.whyImportant: It defined how labs ship models with dangerous dual-use skills without a single open release.
narrative.problemSolved: Frontier cyber and biology capability needed deployment paths for defenders, not just blanket refusals.

events.title: Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 access suspended
events.summary: On June 12, 2026, a U.S. export-control directive forced Anthropic to disable Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for all users worldwide — three days after launch.
events.about: The Commerce Department barred foreign nationals from using Fable and Mythos, including Anthropic's own non-citizen staff. With no way to filter users by nationality in real time, Anthropic pulled both models globally. Washington cited a reported Fable 5 jailbreak; Anthropic disputed the severity. Access was restored July 1 after controls were lifted.

narrative.whyChosen: The first export-control shutdown of a deployed commercial frontier AI model.
narrative.whyImportant: It proved governments could block frontier models post-launch, not just restrict chips.
narrative.problemSolved: National security officials needed a mechanism to limit foreign access to dual-use AI systems.

events.title: Anthropic: Fable 5 "could be misused to cause serious damage"
events.quoteText: Without safeguards, Fable 5's capabilities in areas like cybersecurity could be misused to cause serious damage.
events.summary: Launching Claude Fable 5, Anthropic warns the model is too capable in offensive cybersecurity to release without safety classifiers.
events.about: Anthropic split Fable 5 from Mythos 5 on day one: same weights, but Fable routes sensitive cyber and biology queries to Opus 4.8. The line justified why a frontier model shipped with guardrails critics called overly broad — and why Mythos stayed locked to Project Glasswing partners.

narrative.whyChosen: Anthropic's own words for why its strongest GA model needed hard blocks on day one.
narrative.whyImportant: It framed dual-use AI risk as a shipping constraint, not just a research talking point.
narrative.problemSolved: Labs needed language for releasing dangerous-capability models without open-weight misuse.

events.title: Anthropic: "We must abruptly disable Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for all our customers"
events.quoteText: The net effect of this order is that we must abruptly disable Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for all our customers to ensure compliance.
events.summary: Three days after launch, a U.S. export-control directive forces Anthropic to pull its frontier models offline worldwide.
events.about: Commerce ordered Anthropic to block foreign nationals from using Fable and Mythos — including employees in the U.S. Because the API could not verify citizenship in real time, Anthropic shut both models off for everyone. The first time Washington used export controls on a deployed commercial frontier model, not just training chips.

narrative.whyChosen: The sentence that turned AI safety rhetoric into a global product blackout.
narrative.whyImportant: It showed governments could recall frontier models days after launch over jailbreak fears.
narrative.problemSolved: Policymakers needed a lever to block foreign access to models deemed nationally sensitive.

events.title: Anthropic: recall standard would "halt all new model deployments"
events.quoteText: If this standard was applied across the industry, we believe it would essentially halt all new model deployments for all frontier model providers.
events.summary: Responding to the Fable 5 shutdown, Anthropic argues a narrow jailbreak finding should not recall models used by hundreds of millions.
events.about: Anthropic complied with the export-control order but disputed the rationale: the reported bypass was narrow, and other frontier models showed similar capability. The pushback previewed an industry fight over when a jailbreak should trigger withdrawal versus patched safeguards.

narrative.whyChosen: Anthropic's counter-argument to the first frontier-model recall order.
narrative.whyImportant: It defined the stakes for every lab shipping cyber-capable models after Fable.
narrative.problemSolved: Industry lacked a shared standard for when a jailbreak should block a model release.
